threatModel.deployment: One club operates one Courtside instance behind the reference proxy with PostgreSQL and server-side sessions.

surfaces.description: Public HTML shell, court plan, static assets and PWA lifecycle.
Login, bootstrap, initial password and brute-force controls.
Server-side sessions, CSRF, logout, expiry and credential changes.
Bookings, series, participants and personal booking data.
Facility, cards, rules and club configuration administration.
People, accounts, roles, memberships and membership types.
CSV snapshots, previews, external references and full synchronization.
Contract-first JSON boundary and RFC 9457 error surface.
Caddy, container runtime, network and PostgreSQL topology.
Candidate image, dependencies, SBOM, provenance and signature.
Logs, metrics, backups, restores and retained evidence.

trustBoundaries.description: Untrusted browser and network traffic enters through Caddy.
Forwarded identity and transport metadata crosses into Spring Boot.
Application data and server-side sessions enter PostgreSQL.
Source and dependencies become a signed container image.
Operational commands create logs, backups and security evidence.

safe.description: Bounded passive and non-destructive checks that do not alter domain state or exhaust resources.

active.description: Curated authentication, authorization, mutation and injection attacks against a disposable target.

destructive.description: Bounded exhaustion and protocol-abuse checks that may make the disposable target unavailable.

passed.description: Every selected control executed with complete evidence and no unaccepted validated finding.

incomplete.description: A tool, prerequisite, target proof, control or required evidence is missing or failed to execute.

failed.description: A secure outcome was violated or a validated finding remains outside an unexpired acceptance.

severity.releasePolicy: Blocks release until fixed and retested.
Blocks release unless an explicit unexpired acceptance records compensating controls.
Requires an owned remediation or time-bounded acceptance.
Recorded and prioritized with product context.

controlEvidence.falsifyingTest: frontend/e2e/browser-security.spec.ts#stored text projections remain inert on administrative and managed views

controls.rationale: The shipped server exposes no request-controlled source-code, include, expression or script interpreter. Courtside compiles Java ahead of startup and serves a prebuilt static TypeScript application, so a request has no server-side code-evaluation sink.

No shipped request path invokes an operating-system command, shell, ProcessBuilder or Runtime.exec. Database setup and application behavior use Java and JDBC APIs directly, leaving no request-controlled command sink to test.

No request value becomes a printf, MessageFormat or database format template. Format strings in the shipped source are constants; the database-provisioning formatter is startup-only and passes environment values as PostgreSQL %I or %L arguments rather than as the format string.

controls.rationale: Courtside ships no server-side HTML template engine and accepts no user-editable template. Mail resource bundles use a bounded named-placeholder replacement to produce plain text, not an executable server template context.

No request selects a server-side network destination. The breach-password client uses a fixed production endpoint and sends only a hash prefix; the SMTP relay and observability targets are operator startup configuration rather than request data, while configured logo links are fetched by the browser.

tests.title: Authentication and brute-force boundaries
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: Invalid and abusive authentication attempts cannot enumerate or take over an account and remain rate limited across path variants.

tests.title: Administrative multi-factor authentication
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: Administrative access requires the documented ASVS Level 2 authentication strength.
tests.rationale: Courtside does not yet provide a second factor for administrators.

tests.title: Session lifecycle and browser isolation
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: Login rotates the session and logout, expiry, password change and authority removal invalidate stale access without browser-history disclosure.

tests.title: Operation, role and object authorization matrix
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: Every operation and object is accessible only to explicitly authorized roles and owners, with rejected attempts leaving state unchanged.

tests.title: Booking integrity under competing and abusive requests
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: Competing writes preserve one occupancy, authorization, participant capacity and idempotency without partial state.

tests.title: Participation consent and personal-data isolation
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: A participant can discover and withdraw only their own participation without resolving another person's identity.

tests.title: Configuration administration boundaries
prerequisites: Existing facility, card and rule resources
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: Only authorized fields and operations can change club configuration, with conflicts and invalid references leaving state unchanged.

tests.title: People, account and membership administration
prerequisites: Synthetic roster with ownership and role boundaries
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: Person, account, role and membership mutations cannot cross role or person boundaries or expose unrelated personal fields.

tests.title: Snapshot parser and synchronization abuse
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: Malformed, oversized, ambiguous and conflicting snapshots cannot escape parsing limits, take over accounts or leave a partial synchronization.

tests.title: Browser injection and client-side data retention
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: Untrusted values remain data, CSP violations are observable and personal data is unavailable from browser storage after session termination.

tests.title: Proxy, TLS and runtime exposure
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: The proxy and runtime expose only intended routes and methods, preserve trusted forwarding boundaries and use the documented TLS and container controls.

tests.title: Source, dependency and candidate-image evidence
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: Required static and dependency evidence is complete, exceptions are current and release attestations bind to the assessed digest.

tests.title: Contract-bound malformed input and error handling
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: Malformed and boundary inputs produce stable typed failures without undocumented routes, unhandled exceptions or partial state.

tests.title: Adversarial resource consumption and recovery
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: Bounded attacker-shaped load stops before host limits, preserves integrity and leaves the service recoverable.

tests.title: Sensitive operational data and recovery evidence
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: Logs, metrics, backups and assessment evidence contain no credentials or unintended personal data and retain sufficient provenance for recovery and investigation.

tests.title: Bounded authenticated dynamic application scan
prerequisites: Pinned ZAP image and rule policy
tests.expectedSecureOutcome: Authenticated discovery and curated active rules remain inside the approved read-only routes, retain every scanner alert as an untriaged candidate and fail closed on lost authentication or coverage.
